newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN EX-ARMY CHIEF SAYS HE FOUGHT GOOD FIGHT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN EX-ARMY CHIEF SAYS HE FOUGHT GOOD FIGHT.

text.p: Former South African Defence Force chief General Constand Viljoen said on Monday he was proud of the way his troops had fought communism during the apartheid era.
Viljoen, now leader of the right-wing Freedom Front party, praised the defence force submission to the country's Truth and Reconciliation earlier in the day as "professional and military".

The deputy chairman of the commission, Alex Boraine, criticised the submission as "breathtakingly one-sided" and said it failed to accept any blame for human rights abuses on behalf of the defence force.

But Viljoen, a leading figure in efforts by rightist Afrikaners to obtain some form of self-rule in South Africa, said the commission's critical response showed only that commission members had no knowledge of "military professionalism".
"We are proud of the effective way in which we carried out our duty to defend our country and keep South Africa free of communism," he said in a statement.
"We are aware of the effect such a revolutionary war had on many innocent people," Viljoen said, adding that two sides had been involved and both had to take part in reconciliation.

He said some actions by his troops and by guerrillas of the African National Congress had resulted in unacceptable human rights abuses, and those involved needed to apply for amnesty regardless of which side they fought on.
